JetBrains plugin manifest dropped under user-writable plugins directory by non-IDE process AIInstallation Medium
Persistence pivot: catches a plugin.xml or META-INF\plugin.xml being written under a per-user JetBrains plugins directory by a process that ISN'T the JetBrains IDE installer itself — useful for catching out-of-band installs (manual disk drops, packaging scripts, malware) that bypass Marketplace flow but still load on next IDE start. Rationale: Catches lateral-movement / sideloading variants of the Aikido campaign — even if the attacker pivots off the Marketplace, the plugin still has to land plugin.xml inside the per-user JetBrains plugins folder to be auto-loaded by the IDE. Excluding the IDE's own binaries narrows to out-of-band writes (script, archive extractor, malware dropper).
ATT&CKT1547.014 T1505.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Developer manually unzipping a plugin from a downloaded .zip (7zip.exe / explorer.exe as ActingProcess)
  • DevOps tooling provisioning plugins via Ansible/Chef/Puppet (likely an agent process)
  • Backup software restoring the plugins directory
  • Custom enterprise plugin distribution scripts
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("msiexec.exe","installer.exe","chef-client.exe","puppet.exe","ansible.exe")
Response runbook
1) TRIAGE: read the dropped plugin.xml — look for the <id> tag and cross-check against the 15 known-malicious IDs (org.sm.yms.toolkit etc.) and any vendor URL that resolves to a non-JetBrains domain. 2) CONTAIN: delete the plugin directory before next IDE start (else it auto-loads) and capture a copy for analysis. 3) HUNT: pivot on ActingProcessName to see what else that process touched on the host; query EDR for the same process writing plugin.xml on any other developer workstation.
let JetBrainsProcs = dynamic(["idea64.exe","idea.exe","pycharm64.exe","webstorm64.exe","phpstorm64.exe","clion64.exe","rider64.exe","goland64.exe","datagrip64.exe","rustrover64.exe","rubymine64.exe","toolbox.exe","appcode.exe","studio64.exe"]);
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName =~ "plugin.xml"
| where FolderPath has "JetBrains" and FolderPath has "plugins"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ (JetBrainsProcs)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, FolderPath, FileName, ActionType
| order by Timestamp desc
let JetBrainsProcs = dynamic(["idea64.exe","idea.exe","pycharm64.exe","webstorm64.exe","phpstorm64.exe","clion64.exe","rider64.exe","goland64.exe","datagrip64.exe","rustrover64.exe","rubymine64.exe","toolbox.exe"]);
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where TargetFileName =~ "plugin.xml"
| where TargetFilePath has "JetBrains" and TargetFilePath has "plugins"
| where ActingProcessName !in~ (JetBrainsProcs)
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFilePath, EventType
| order by TimeGenerated desc

| regex("(?i)\\\\JetBrains\\\\.+\\\\plugins\\\\.+\\\\plugin\\.xml$", field=TargetFileName)
| NOT ContextImageFileName=/\\(idea64|idea|pycharm64|webstorm64|phpstorm64|clion64|rider64|goland64|datagrip64|rustrover64|rubymine64|toolbox)\.exe$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ContextImageFileName, TargetFileName], function=count())

Suspicious browser extension installation Installation Medium
Side-loaded / unsigned extensions, often masquerading as wallets, productivity tools.
ATT&CKT1176

Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs Actions on Objectives High

2026-06-17 5 use cases 4 techniques 5 kill-chain phases detected

Breaches don't always start with a zero-day. An exposed admin panel can get brute-forced, or credentials reused from a previous attack. But when a vulnerability does drop — like MongoBleed earlier this year, which let attackers pull credentials and session tokens from server memory without authentication — anything internet-facing is immediately at risk. Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration. → Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code.
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key.
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking.
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs · Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change · LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) · Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement

Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies SQLite from Chrome/Edge/Firefox.

| where Timestamp > ago(7d)

| where FileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")

Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s) Reconnaissance High
Match vulnerability scanner output to the CVE(s) named in the article.
ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesVulnerabilities DeviceInfo DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine
// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2025-14847")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,
// `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities` is available. Otherwise this UC has
// no Sentinel translation — track via Update / Heartbeat OS-version
// gaps as a coarse approximation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2025-14847")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,
          VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc
APPLICATION
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Vulnerabilities
    where Vulnerabilities.signature IN ("CVE-2025-14847")
    by Vulnerabilities.dest, Vulnerabilities.signature, Vulnerabilities.severity, Vulnerabilities.cve
| `drop_dm_object_name(Vulnerabilities)`
| sort - severity
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Vulnerabilities
    where Vulnerabilities.signature IN ("CVE-2025-14847")
    by Vulnerabilities.dest, Vulnerabilities.signature, Vulnerabilities.severity, Vulnerabilities.cve
| `drop_dm_object_name(Vulnerabilities)`
| sort - severity
Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change Actions on Objectives Medium
Threshold detection: many files renamed in short window, often with new extension.
ATT&CKT1486
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(FileName) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, bin(Timestamp, 1m)
| where files > 200    // empirical: > 200 unique-file renames in 1m by one account on one host
                       //            is well above the P99 of legitimate bulk-tooling
| order by files desc

ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where EventType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(TargetFileName)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)
| where files > 200    // P99 of legit bulk-tooling per-minute rename volume
| order by files desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
| tstats summariesonly=false count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) Actions on Objectives High
Mimikatz, comsvcs.dll MiniDump, or any non-Windows process opening LSASS.
ATT&CKT1003.001 T1003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall"
| where FileName =~ "lsass.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","csrss.exe",
                                          "svchost.exe","wininit.exe","services.exe",
                                          "lsm.exe","SearchProtocolHost.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, AccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
// SecurityEvent EventID 4663 = object access. AccessMask 0x10 / 0x40 / 0x1010
// indicate read access to lsass.exe — credential-dump signature. Audit
// Object Access > Audit File System policy required.
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,
          AccessMask, AccessReason
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: PsExec / SMB Lateral Movement Tooling Execution
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d03
status: experimental
description: |
    PsExec, paexec, smbexec, csexec, remcom — admin-grade tooling that
    pivots over SMB. Pair with `wmic /node:` for the full cluster.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1021/002/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1569/002/
author: Clankerusecase

Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] npm install referencing compromised @mastra packages or easy-day-js dependency
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] easy-day-js postinstall hook running node setup.cjs --no-warnings · [LLM] Node spawning detached script from %TEMP% with 24-hex filename and host:port argv (stage-2) · Suspicious browser extension installation
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] Outbound HTTPS to Mastra supply-chain C2 23.254.164.92:8000 and 23.254.164.123:443 · Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] Mastra dropper beacon file .pkg_history/.pkg_logs created by node in temp directory · [LLM] node.exe reading developer credential files shortly after npm install (Mastra stage-2) · Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs · Crypto-wallet file/keystore access by non-wallet process
easy-day-js postinstall hook running node setup.cjs --no-warnings AIInstallation High
Detects the @mastra supply-chain dropper's entry point: a node.exe process executing setup.cjs with the warning-suppression flag, almost always spawned from an npm/npx/yarn parent during package install. The string pair is unique to this campaign. Rationale: The literal cmdline pair 'setup.cjs' + '--no-warnings' is the postinstall hook defined in the malicious easy-day-js@1.11.22 package.json verbatim from the article. Combined with an npm/npx/yarn parent it has no legitimate analog in production environments. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/issues/18045 • https://app.stepsecurity.io/oss-security-feed/@mastra/schema-compat?version=1.2.12
ATT&CKT1059.007 T1546.016 T1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Developer-written test fixture literally named setup.cjs in an internal package's postinstall
  • Internal Node.js tooling that happens to chain --no-warnings into a build script called setup.cjs
  • Security research labs detonating the IOC sample for analysis
  • Vendored npm modules where a maintainer reused the filename setup.cjs for legitimate bootstrap
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("jest","mocha","vitest","--test") and ProcessCommandLine !contains "easy-day-js")
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the host's npm/yarn lockfile and confirm if easy-day-js@1.11.22 or any @mastra package version listed in the article is resolved. Capture SHA256 of the setup.cjs file and compare against IOCs 221c45a7…, 4a886024…, ae70dd4f…. 2) Contain: isolate the host (developer workstation or CI runner), revoke any NPM_TOKEN/GITHUB_TOKEN/ANTHROPIC_API_KEY/OPENAI_API_KEY/AWS keys present on the box, kill any node child process still running, force-rotate org-level npm publish tokens. 3) Hunt: pivot on InitiatingProcessAccountName + DeviceId to find any node child writing to %TEMP%\<24-hex>.js, any connection to 23.254.164.0/24, and any reads of ~/.aws/credentials, ~/.npmrc, or .github/workflows secrets directories in the 60 minutes following the postinstall.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName in~ ("node.exe","node")
| where ProcessCommandLine has "setup.cjs" and ProcessCommandLine has "--no-warnings"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("npm.exe","npm","npm-cli.js","npx.exe","npx","node.exe","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe","cmd.exe","bash","sh")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, FolderPath, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where NewProcessName endswith "\\node.exe" or NewProcessName endswith "/node"
| where CommandLine has "setup.cjs" and CommandLine has "--no-warnings"
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("npm.exe","npm-cli.js","npx.exe","node.exe","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe","cmd.exe","bash","sh")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Outbound HTTPS to Mastra supply-chain C2 23.254.164.92:8000 and 23.254.164.123:443 AICommand & Control Medium
Alerts on any host (dev workstation or CI runner) connecting to the stage-1 download server 23.254.164.92:8000 or stage-2 exfil server 23.254.164.123:443, including their hostwinds DNS aliases. These IPs and the /update/<numeric-id> URI shape are unique to this campaign. Rationale: Both /24-adjacent IPs and both hostwinds aliases are explicit IOCs in the article body and kill-chain reconstruction. The /update/49890878 URI path is the literal stage-1 endpoint copied verbatim from the article. Any hit is a high-fidelity infection indicator. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/issues/18045 • https://app.stepsecurity.io/oss-security-feed/@mastra/schema-compat?version=1.2.12
ATT&CKT1105 T1071.001 T1571 T1041
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Web.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Threat intelligence analysts manually visiting the C2 from a sandbox
  • Internal blue-team red-team exercises replaying the IOC list
  • Internet-wide scanners (Censys, Shodan, Project Discovery) operating from corporate egress
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("WindowsSandboxClient.exe","sandbox.exe")
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the InitiatingProcessFileName for the connection — if it's node.exe with a parent of npm/npx/yarn, treat as confirmed Mastra supply-chain infection. Capture the full lockfile and resolved easy-day-js / @mastra package versions. 2) Contain: block 23.254.164.0/24 and both hwsrv-1327785/6.hostwindsdns.com at perimeter and proxy, isolate any host that connected, kill all node child processes. 3) Hunt: rotate every secret accessible from that host: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, OPENAI_API_KEY, AWS keys, GITHUB_TOKEN, NPM_TOKEN. Search SigninLogs / CloudTrail / GitHub audit log for any use of those tokens from non-corporate IPs in the 24h window starting at the first connection.
let badIPs = dynamic(["23.254.164.92","23.254.164.123"]);
let badDomains = dynamic(["hwsrv-1327786.hostwindsdns.com","hwsrv-1327785.hostwindsdns.com"]);
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteIP in (badIPs)
   or RemoteUrl has_any (badDomains)
   or RemoteUrl has "/update/49890878"
| extend Stage = case(RemoteIP == "23.254.164.92" or RemoteUrl has "hwsrv-1327786", "Stage1-Download",
                     RemoteIP == "23.254.164.123" or RemoteUrl has "hwsrv-1327785", "Stage2-Exfil", "Unknown")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, Stage, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl, InitiatingProcessFolderPath
| order by Timestamp desc

Node spawning detached script from %TEMP% with 24-hex filename and host:port argv (stage-2) AIInstallation High
Hunts the stage-2 execution shape unique to this dropper: node.exe launching a script whose basename matches ^[a-f0-9]{24}\.js$ located in the OS temp directory, with the stage-2 C2 host:port (e.g. 23.254.164.123:443) passed as the second argv. This combination is artifact-driven and has no legitimate analog. Rationale: The 24-hex-char .js filename in tmpdir and host:port argv pattern come directly from the kill-chain reconstruction's quoted spawn signature: child_process.spawn(process.execPath, [filepath, stage2C2], {cwd: os.tmpdir(), detached: true}). Both the filename shape and the trailing host:port argv are highly specific.
ATT&CKT1059.007 T1105 T1564.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • npm pack/install creating randomly-named cache files that happen to match the 24-hex pattern (rare — npm uses longer hashes)
  • Internal build tools generating obfuscated cache files in TEMP
  • Electron app updaters writing temp staging scripts (typically named app-update.js etc., not bare hex)
Response runbook
1) Triage: extract the Stage2Target column — if it resolves to 23.254.164.0/24 or hwsrv-1327785.hostwindsdns.com, treat as confirmed Mastra C2 callback. Capture the .js file from %TEMP% before it self-deletes. 2) Contain: isolate the host, kill the detached node process tree, preserve %TEMP% contents for forensics, block stage-2 IP/domain at perimeter. 3) Hunt: enumerate every secret on the host (env vars, ~/.aws, ~/.npmrc, ~/.config/gh, GitHub Actions runner secrets), assume compromised, rotate. Pivot on the package.json that pulled in easy-day-js to identify other infected hosts.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName in~ ("node.exe","node")
| where ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(?:\\Temp\\|AppData\\Local\\Temp\\|/tmp/)[a-f0-9]{24}\.js\s+\S+:\d{2,5}"
| extend Stage2Target = extract(@"([a-zA-Z0-9\.\-]+:\d{2,5})\s*$", 1, ProcessCommandLine)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine, Stage2Target, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where NewProcessName endswith "\\node.exe" or NewProcessName endswith "/node"
| where CommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(?:\\Temp\\|AppData\\Local\\Temp\\|/tmp/)[a-f0-9]{24}\.js\s+\S+:\d{2,5}"
| extend Stage2Target = extract(@"([a-zA-Z0-9\.\-]+:\d{2,5})\s*$", 1, CommandLine)
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine, Stage2Target, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ImageFileName=/\\node\.exe$/i
| regex("(?i)(\\\\Temp\\\\|AppData\\\\Local\\\\Temp\\\\|/tmp/)[a-f0-9]{24}\\.js\\s+\\S+:\\d{2,5}", field=CommandLine)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, CommandLine, SHA256HashData], function=count())

npm install referencing compromised @mastra packages or easy-day-js dependency AIDelivery High
Hunts hosts and CI runners executing npm/yarn/pnpm install that explicitly name easy-day-js or one of the 13 compromised @mastra package versions. Catches both intentional installs and those triggered by lockfile updates that resolved during the 36-minute attack window on 2026-06-17. Rationale: The full list of 13 compromised @mastra packages plus the easy-day-js typosquat dependency name come directly from the article's affected-versions table. Any command-line reference is article-specific by definition — this name was registered as a typosquat purely for this campaign. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/issues/18045
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1199
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Security-aware developers running `npm view easy-day-js` to inspect the IOC
  • Incident-response forensic captures of infected lockfiles being read on analyst workstations
  • Mastra framework users who legitimately depend on @mastra/core but pinned to versions BEFORE 1.42.1 (the malicious release)
  • SCA tooling like socket.dev or snyk scanning package metadata
Suppression filter
| where ProcessCommandLine !has_any ("npm view","npm info","npm search","socket.dev","snyk","--dry-run")
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm the host's package-lock.json/yarn.lock actually RESOLVED easy-day-js@1.11.22 (cmdline can name a package without installing the malicious version if pinned). Check resolved version, not declared range. 2) Contain: if the malicious version is resolved, isolate, rotate every secret accessible from that host (LLM keys, AWS, GitHub, NPM), purge node_modules and lockfile, force-pin @mastra packages to known-good versions. 3) Hunt: query CI/CD systems for any pipeline run between 2026-06-17 01:01 UTC and present that did `npm install` for any of the 13 affected packages — those builds installed the malicious dependency and any secrets in the runner environment must be considered burned.

DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName in~ ("npm.exe","npm","npx.exe","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe","node.exe") or InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("npm.exe","npm","npx.exe","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any (compromised) or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any (compromised)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FolderPath

| where CommandLine has_any (compromised)

Mastra dropper beacon file .pkg_history/.pkg_logs created by node in temp directory AIActions on Objectives High
Detects creation of the campaign's victim-fingerprint files (.pkg_history, .pkg_logs) written to the OS temp directory by a node.exe process. These filenames are unique to the easy-day-js dropper and are used to record install path and compromised package name. Rationale: The .pkg_history and .pkg_logs file names in temp are explicit IOCs from the kill-chain reconstruction's quoted detection hint: 'Beacon: record install path and package name in tmp dir'. These dotfile names with that path constraint and node.exe writer have no benign analog.
ATT&CKT1083 T1005
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Custom internal npm tooling that happens to write a similarly-named beacon file
  • Other npm packages legitimately using .pkg_history (none known)
  • Forensic capture replay during IR exercises
Response runbook
1) Triage: read the contents of the .pkg_history / .pkg_logs file to confirm it lists @mastra package paths and easy-day-js. Capture the file before the dropper self-cleans. 2) Contain: isolate the host, kill any node child, block 23.254.164.0/24 at egress, preserve %TEMP% for forensics. 3) Hunt: pivot on InitiatingProcessAccountName + DeviceId — query the previous 30 days of DeviceProcessEvents for the postinstall hook (UC1) and DeviceNetworkEvents for the C2 IPs (UC2) to scope the dwell time. Treat any secret accessible from this host as burned and rotate.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ActionType == "FileCreated"
| where FileName in~ (".pkg_history",".pkg_logs")
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\Temp\", "/tmp/", @"AppData\Local\Temp")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node.exe","node")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FileName, FolderPath, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventType == "FileCreated"
| where TargetFileName in~ (".pkg_history",".pkg_logs")
| where TargetFilePath has_any (@"\Temp\", "/tmp/", @"AppData\Local\Temp")
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("node.exe","node")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Mastra Dropper Beacon File .pkg_history/.pkg_logs in Temp
id: 4a2b8c1d-9e3f-4b5a-87d2-1f6a3c4e9b21
description: Detects the easy-day-js dropper writing its victim-fingerprint files (.pkg_history / .pkg_logs) into the OS temp directory
references:

author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/17
tags:
  - attack.t1083
  - attack.t1005
  - attack.t1195.002
logsource:
  category: file_event
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_name:
    TargetFilename|endswith:
      - '\.pkg_history'
      - '\.pkg_logs'

level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:11 @TargetFilename:(*\\Temp\\.pkg_history OR *\\Temp\\.pkg_logs OR *AppData\\Local\\Temp\\.pkg_history OR *AppData\\Local\\Temp\\.pkg_logs OR */tmp/.pkg_history OR */tmp/.pkg_logs) @Image:(*\\node.exe OR *\\Node.exe OR *\\NODE.EXE)
#event_simpleName=FileWritten ContextImageFileName=/\\node\.exe$/i TargetFileName=/(\\Temp\\|AppData\\Local\\Temp\\|\/tmp\/)\.(pkg_history|pkg_logs)$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, TargetFileName, ContextImageFileName], function=count())

node.exe reading developer credential files shortly after npm install (Mastra stage-2) AIActions on Objectives Medium
Hunts the stage-2 credential harvest behaviour: a node.exe process reading ~/.aws/credentials, ~/.config/gh/hosts.yml, or the GitHub Actions runner secrets directory shortly after an npm install. Aligns with the article's assessment that the dropper steals LLM/cloud/VCS tokens for exfil to 23.254.164.123:443. Rationale: Credential file paths (~/.aws/credentials, ~/.config/gh, GitHub Actions runner _temp dir, .npmrc) are from the kill-chain reconstruction's phase 8 quoted hint. The 10-minute join after npm install scopes to the dropper's actual execution window, cutting false positives from cloud-CLI tooling that legitimately reads these files at other times.
ATT&CKT1552.001 T1552.005 T1083
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • aws-cli wrappers shelling out to node and immediately reading ~/.aws/credentials
  • Vercel/Netlify deploy CLI authenticated via gh token reading hosts.yml during build
  • Internal CI bootstrappers that read .npmrc as a normal part of npm install (would need refinement to filter)
  • Electron-based dev tools indexing user dotfiles for autocomplete
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine !has_any ("aws-sdk","@aws-sdk","vercel","netlify","firebase-tools")
Response runbook
1) Triage: cross-reference DeviceName + AccountName against UC4 hits (compromised @mastra install) and UC2 hits (C2 callback). Three-way correlation = high-confidence credential theft. 2) Contain: force-rotate every cred read by node — AWS keys in ~/.aws, GitHub PAT in ~/.config/gh, NPM publish tokens in ~/.npmrc, SSH keys. For CI runners, revoke runner registration tokens and re-provision. 3) Hunt: pivot the stolen credentials to CloudTrail/AzureActivity/GitHub audit log — search for the rotated AWS access key's last-used location, any unfamiliar IPs on the GitHub token usage, and any new npm publish events under the developer's account in the 24h post-infection window.
let CredentialReads = DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node.exe","node")
| where (FolderPath has @"\.aws\" and FileName == "credentials")
    or (FolderPath has "/.aws/" and FileName == "credentials")
    or (FolderPath has @"\.config\gh\" and FileName == "hosts.yml")
    or (FolderPath has "/.config/gh/" and FileName == "hosts.yml")
    or (FolderPath has @"\.ssh\" and FileName matches regex @"^id_(rsa|ed25519|ecdsa)$")
    or (FolderPath has "Runner.Worker" and FolderPath has "_temp")
    or FileName =~ ".npmrc";
let RecentNpmInstall = DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ProcessCommandLine has "npm" and ProcessCommandLine has "install"
| project NpmTime = Timestamp, DeviceId, NpmUser = AccountName;
CredentialReads
| join kind=inner RecentNpmInstall on DeviceId
| where Timestamp between (NpmTime .. NpmTime + 10m)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, NpmTime, DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, NpmTime), InitiatingProcessAccountName, FolderPath, FileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
let CredReads = ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("node.exe","node")
| where (TargetFilePath has @"\.aws\" and TargetFileName == "credentials")
    or (TargetFilePath has "/.aws/" and TargetFileName == "credentials")
    or (TargetFilePath has @"\.config\gh\" and TargetFileName == "hosts.yml")
    or (TargetFilePath has "/.config/gh/" and TargetFileName == "hosts.yml")
    or TargetFileName =~ ".npmrc"
    or (TargetFilePath has "Runner.Worker" and TargetFilePath has "_temp");
let NpmRuns = ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has "npm" and ActingProcessCommandLine has "install"
| project NpmTime = TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, NpmUser = ActorUsername;
CredReads
| join kind=inner NpmRuns on DvcHostname
| where TimeGenerated between (NpmTime .. NpmTime + 10m)
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, NpmTime, DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', TimeGenerated, NpmTime), ActorUsername, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:11 @Image:(*\\node.exe OR *\\Node.exe OR *\\NODE.EXE) @TargetFilename:(*\\.aws\\credentials OR */.aws/credentials OR *\\.config\\gh\\hosts.yml OR */.config/gh/hosts.yml OR *\\.ssh\\id_rsa OR */.ssh/id_rsa OR *Runner.Worker*_temp*)
#event_simpleName=FileOpenInfo ContextImageFileName=/\\node\.exe$/i
| regex("(\\\\\\.aws\\\\credentials|/\\.aws/credentials|\\\\\\.config\\\\gh\\\\hosts\\.yml|/\\.config/gh/hosts\\.yml|\\\\\\.ssh\\\\id_(rsa|ed25519|ecdsa)|Runner\\.Worker.*_temp)", field=TargetFileName)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, TargetFileName], function=count())
ENDPOINT

| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Filesystem.file_path) as paths values(Filesystem.process_name) as proc from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where Filesystem.process_name=node.exe (Filesystem.file_path="*\\.aws\\credentials*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.aws/credentials*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\.config\\gh\\hosts.yml*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.config/gh/hosts.yml*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\.ssh\\id_rsa*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.ssh/id_rsa*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*Runner.Worker*secret*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*_temp\\_runner_file_commands*") by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Filesystem.file_path) as paths values(Filesystem.process_name) as proc from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where Filesystem.process_name=node.exe (Filesystem.file_path="*\\.aws\\credentials*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.aws/credentials*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\.config\\gh\\hosts.yml*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.config/gh/hosts.yml*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\.ssh\\id_rsa*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.ssh/id_rsa*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*Runner.Worker*secret*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*_temp\\_runner_file_commands*") by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
Network connections to article IPs / domains Command & Control High
Outbound traffic to attacker infrastructure named in the article.
ATT&CKT1071
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Web Network_Resolution.DNS DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemoteIP in ("23.254.164.92", "23.254.164.123") or RemoteUrl has_any ("https://23.254.164.92:8000/update/49890878", "https://23.254.164.123:443/49890878")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
let BadIPs     = dynamic(["23.254.164.92", "23.254.164.123"]);
let BadDomains = dynamic(["https://23.254.164.92:8000/update/49890878", "https://23.254.164.123:443/49890878"]);
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where DstIpAddr in (BadIPs)
   or Url has_any (BadDomains)
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, Url, NetworkProtocol
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs Actions on Objectives High
Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies SQLite from Chrome/Edge/Firefox.
ATT&CKT1539 T1555.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\", @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\", @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where FileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FolderPath, FileName, ActionType

// ASIM ImFileEvent — covers MDE, Sysmon, AuditD, Defender for Cloud, etc.
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where TargetFilePath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\",
                                  @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\",
                                  @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where TargetFileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where ActingProcessName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName,
          TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, EventType

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:

Joomla JCE Component Exploitation Attempt (CVE-2026-48907) AIExploitation High
Hunts unauthenticated HTTP requests targeting the Joomla Content Editor (JCE) component endpoints, specifically /components/com_jce/ and editor profile creation paths exploited via CVE-2026-48907 for PHP upload. Targets the access-control bypass that allows unauthenticated editor-profile creation leading to arbitrary PHP upload. Rationale: Targets the exact vulnerable component path (com_jce) and editor-profile endpoint named in the CVE.org description for CVE-2026-48907. Pre-patch JCE versions 1.0.0-2.9.99.4 expose these paths to unauthenticated editor-profile creation. Cross-checked against: • https://www.cisa.gov/known-exploited-vulnerabilities-catalog • https://www.joomlacontenteditor.net/news
ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Joomla site admins legitimately accessing JCE plugin configuration from corporate IPs
  • Automated Joomla update checks polling component endpoints
  • Vulnerability scanners (Nessus, Qualys) probing /components/com_jce/ during authorised assessments
  • Cached/CDN edge prefetch of Joomla admin pages
  • Penetration testers in scope for the engagement
Suppression filter
| where not(cIP in ("<corp-admin-IPs>","<vuln-scanner-IPs>")) and csUserAgent !contains "Nessus" and csUserAgent !contains "Qualys"
Response runbook
Step 1 (Triage): Identify the source IP, geolocation, and reputation. Pull the full URL chain — look for editor/profiles creation, file-manager invocation, or imgmanager plugin abuse. Check the response sizes and Content-Type of the response. Step 2 (Contain): If exploitation is confirmed (HTTP 200 to a profile-creation POST followed by .php write), block the source IP at the WAF/edge, isolate the affected web server, and snapshot for forensics. Verify JCE version — if <= 2.9.99.4, schedule emergency upgrade to 2.9.99.5. Step 3 (Hunt): Search for subsequent file writes to /images/, /tmp/, or webroot of .php files (UC #3), w3wp/php-cgi spawning shells (UC #2), and lateral pivots from the web server. Pull all CVE-2026-48907 inventory hits (UC #4).
// Defender does not natively ingest IIS/Apache HTTP logs; pivot via DeviceNetworkEvents to web-server processes
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("httpd.exe","nginx.exe","w3wp.exe","php-cgi.exe","apache.exe")
| where RemoteUrl has_any ("/components/com_jce/","com_jce","editor/profiles","task=plugin","plugin=imgmanager")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteIP, RemoteUrl, RemotePort
| order by Timestamp desc
let CVE = "CVE-2026-48907";
let JcePaths = dynamic(["/components/com_jce/","com_jce","editor/profiles","task=plugin","plugin=imgmanager","index.php?option=com_jce"]);
(union isfuzzy=true
  (W3CIISLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where csUriStem has_any (JcePaths) or csUriQuery has_any (JcePaths)
    | where scStatus between (200 .. 399)
    | project TimeGenerated, Computer, cIP, csMethod, csUriStem, csUriQuery, scStatus, csUserAgent),
  (CommonSecurityLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where RequestURL has_any (JcePaths)
    | project TimeGenerated, DeviceVendor, DeviceProduct, SourceIP, DestinationHostName, RequestURL, RequestMethod, DeviceAction))
| extend cve = CVE
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Web Service Process Spawning Shell or LOLBin (Post-RCE Webshell Execution) AIExploitation High
Detects w3wp.exe, httpd.exe, nginx.exe, or php-cgi.exe spawning cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash, or LOLBin children — the classic post-exploitation pattern after a webshell drop following CVE-2026-48907 PHP code execution on a Joomla server. Rationale: Article confirms 'PHP Code Execution' as the impact of CVE-2026-48907. The web-service-spawning-shell parent/child relationship is the canonical signal that webshell execution has succeeded. Removed the non-existent IsInitiatingProcessRemoteSession field per validation feedback. Cross-checked against: • https://www.cisa.gov/known-exploited-vulnerabilities-catalog
ATT&CKT1059.002 T1505.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • WordPress/Joomla auto-update scripts invoking shell utilities
  • Web application cron jobs running via PHP exec()
  • PHP-based deployment hooks (Capistrano, Deployer) running git/composer
  • Monitoring agents (PRTG, Zabbix) invoked by the web tier
  • Developer-installed CI runners on web hosts during build
Suppression filter
| where not(ProcessCommandLine has_any ("composer","git pull","wp-cli","joomla-cli","drush")) and AccountName !in~ ("deploy","jenkins","gitlab-runner")
Response runbook
Step 1 (Triage): Capture the full process tree from w3wp/httpd → child, including command line and working directory. Inspect recent .php file writes under the web root in the last 15 minutes. Step 2 (Contain): Isolate the web host from the network, snapshot memory and disk, and disable the web service. Rotate any credentials accessible from the host (DB connection strings in PHP config files). Step 3 (Hunt): Pivot on the source IP from access logs to find related JCE exploitation attempts (UC #1). Check for outbound C2 to 84.201.6.54 or tidio.cc. Search other Joomla hosts in inventory for similar spawn patterns.

| where Timestamp > ago(7d)

title: Web Service Process Spawning Shell or LOLBin
id: 6b2e0a83-4ad2-4f0e-b6f0-1a4d2e9f3b02
description: Detects classic web-RCE post-exploitation where httpd/nginx/php-cgi/w3wp spawn shells or recon LOLBins, typical of Joomla CVE-2026-48907 webshell execution.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/cisa-warns-of-actively-exploited-joomla.html
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/19
tags:
  - attack.t1059.002
  - attack.t1505.003
  - attack.execution
logsource:
  category: process_creation
detection:
  parent:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '\w3wp.exe'
      - '\httpd.exe'
      - '\nginx.exe'
      - '\php-cgi.exe'
      - '\php.exe'
      - '\apache.exe'
      - '/apache2'
      - '/httpd'
      - '/nginx'
      - '/php-fpm'
  child:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\cmd.exe'
      - '\powershell.exe'
      - '\pwsh.exe'
      - '\certutil.exe'
      - '\bitsadmin.exe'
      - '\curl.exe'
      - '\wget.exe'
      - '\whoami.exe'
      - '\net.exe'
      - '/sh'
      - '/bash'
      - '/dash'
  condition: parent and child
level: high
(source:windows.sysmon OR source:linux.auditd) (@ParentImage:(*\w3wp.exe OR *\W3WP.EXE OR *\httpd.exe OR *\HTTPD.EXE OR *\nginx.exe OR *\php-cgi.exe OR *\php.exe OR */apache2 OR */httpd OR */nginx OR */php-fpm) OR @process.parent.executable.path:(*\/apache2 OR *\/httpd OR *\/nginx OR *\/php-fpm)) (@Image:(*\cmd.exe OR *\powershell.exe OR *\pwsh.exe OR *\certutil.exe OR *\bitsadmin.exe OR *\curl.exe OR *\wget.exe OR *\whoami.exe OR *\net.exe) OR @process.executable.path:(*/sh OR */bash OR */dash OR */curl OR */wget OR */whoami))
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ParentBaseFileName=/^(w3wp|httpd|nginx|apache|apache2|php-cgi|php-fpm|php)(\.exe)?$/i ImageFileName=/(cmd|powershell|pwsh|certutil|bitsadmin|curl|wget|whoami|net|ipconfig|systeminfo|sh|bash|dash)(\.exe)?$/i | groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ParentBaseFileName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as cmdlines values(Processes.process_path) as paths from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("w3wp.exe","httpd.exe","nginx.exe","php-cgi.exe","php.exe","apache.exe","apache2") AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","sh","bash","dash","certutil.exe","bitsadmin.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe","whoami.exe","net.exe","ipconfig.exe","systeminfo.exe") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_name Processes.process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as cmdlines values(Processes.process_path) as paths from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("w3wp.exe","httpd.exe","nginx.exe","php-cgi.exe","php.exe","apache.exe","apache2") AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","sh","bash","dash","certutil.exe","bitsadmin.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe","whoami.exe","net.exe","ipconfig.exe","systeminfo.exe") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_name Processes.process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
PHP Webshell File Drop in Joomla Webroot (com_jce / images / tmp) AIInstallation High
Detects creation of .php, .phtml, or .php5 files inside Joomla-writable directories (/components/com_jce/, /images/, /tmp/, /media/) by the web service account — the post-exploitation persistence pattern following CVE-2026-48907 unauthenticated upload. Rationale: Article describes upload+execution of PHP code via JCE editor profile creation. The .php file write into known JCE-writable paths by the web service account is the durable forensic artefact of successful CVE-2026-48907 exploitation. Cross-checked against: • https://www.cisa.gov/known-exploited-vulnerabilities-catalog
ATT&CKT1505.003 T1105
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate Joomla extension installer copying .php files into components
  • Site admin uploading new template via JCE file manager (authenticated)
  • Joomla core update writing component .php files (rare; usually via package manager)
  • Backup-restore tools (Akeeba) extracting site archives into /tmp/
  • Composer/git deployment writing PHP into web root
Suppression filter
| where not(InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("composer install","composer update","akeeba","joomla-cli","installer.php")) and not(FolderPath has "administrator/components")
Response runbook
Step 1 (Triage): Inspect the dropped .php file — look for short obfuscated payloads (eval(base64_decode()), system($_REQUEST[...])), out-of-place file ownership, and timestamps inconsistent with deployment windows. Compare hash against known webshell hashes (China Chopper, WSO, b374k, JCE-specific shells). Step 2 (Contain): Quarantine the file, take a memory snapshot of php-fpm/w3wp, block the dropping source IP at the WAF, and revoke any web-server-readable credentials. Step 3 (Hunt): Pivot file SHA256 to other hosts in fleet. Search access logs for GET/POST to the dropped filename. Run UC #2 for shell spawn from that web host. Inventory JCE versions across estate (UC #4) and emergency-patch any <= 2.9.99.4.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType == "FileCreated"
| where FileName endswith ".php" or FileName endswith ".phtml" or FileName endswith ".php5" or FileName endswith ".phar"
| where FolderPath has_any ("\\components\\com_jce\\","\\images\\","\\tmp\\","\\media\\","/components/com_jce/","/images/","/tmp/","/media/")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("w3wp.exe","httpd.exe","nginx.exe","php-cgi.exe","php.exe","apache.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FolderPath, FileName, SHA256,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventType == "FileCreated"
| where TargetFileExtension in~ ("php","phtml","php5","phar")
| where TargetFilePath has_any ("/components/com_jce/","/images/","/tmp/","/media/","\\components\\com_jce\\","\\images\\","\\tmp\\")
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("w3wp.exe","httpd.exe","nginx.exe","php-cgi.exe","php.exe","apache.exe","apache2","php-fpm")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFileSHA256
title: PHP Webshell File Drop in Joomla Webroot
id: 8c3f2b91-7d6e-4a3d-b1c2-3e7a9b1f2c03
description: Detects the web server writing .php/.phtml files into JCE-writable directories — webshell drop following CVE-2026-48907 exploitation.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/cisa-warns-of-actively-exploited-joomla.html
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/19
tags:
  - attack.t1505.003
  - attack.persistence
logsource:
  category: file_event
detection:
  selection_process:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\w3wp.exe'
      - '\httpd.exe'
      - '\nginx.exe'
      - '\php-cgi.exe'
      - '\php.exe'
      - '/apache2'
      - '/httpd'
      - '/php-fpm'
  selection_file:

      - '/components/com_jce/'

  condition: selection_process and selection_file
level: high
(source:windows.sysmon OR source:linux.auditd) @EventID:11 @TargetFilename:(*\/components\/com_jce\/*.php OR *\/components\/com_jce\/*.phtml OR *\/images\/*.php OR *\/tmp\/*.php OR *\/media\/*.php OR *\\components\\com_jce\\*.php) @Image:(*\w3wp.exe OR *\httpd.exe OR *\nginx.exe OR *\php-cgi.exe OR */apache2 OR */php-fpm)
#event_simpleName=FileWritten TargetFileName=/\.(php|phtml|php5|phar)$/i TargetFileName=/(components\/com_jce\/|\/images\/|\/tmp\/|\/media\/|components\\com_jce\\)/i ContextImageFileName=/(w3wp|httpd|nginx|apache|apache2|php-cgi|php-fpm|php)(\.exe)?$/i | groupBy([aid, ComputerName, TargetFileName, ContextImageFileName], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Filesystem.user) as users values(Filesystem.process_name) as procs from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where Filesystem.action=created AND (Filesystem.file_name="*.php" OR Filesystem.file_name="*.phtml" OR Filesystem.file_name="*.php5" OR Filesystem.file_name="*.phar") AND (Filesystem.file_path="*/components/com_jce/*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/images/*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/tmp/*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/media/*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\components\\com_jce\\*") by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.file_path Filesystem.file_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Filesystem.user) as users values(Filesystem.process_name) as procs from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where Filesystem.action=created AND (Filesystem.file_name="*.php" OR Filesystem.file_name="*.phtml" OR Filesystem.file_name="*.php5" OR Filesystem.file_name="*.phar") AND (Filesystem.file_path="*/components/com_jce/*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/images/*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/tmp/*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/media/*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\components\\com_jce\\*") by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.file_path Filesystem.file_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
Vulnerable Joomla JCE Version Inventory (CVE-2026-48907) AIReconnaissance High
Hunting query against Defender TVM software inventory to surface Joomla servers running JCE between 1.0.0 and 2.9.99.4 — the vulnerable range patched in 2.9.99.5 (released 2026-06-03). Used to scope exposure ahead of CISA's 2026-06-19 FCEB remediation deadline. Rationale: Article specifies exact vulnerable range (1.0.0 through 2.9.99.4), patched version (2.9.99.5), patch date (2026-06-03), and CISA KEV remediation deadline (2026-06-19). Asset-matching this range with internet-facing exposure surfaces the exact prioritisation list. Cross-checked against: • https://www.cisa.gov/known-exploited-vulnerabilities-catalog • https://www.joomlacontenteditor.net/news
ATT&CKT1190
Data sources
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Test/staging Joomla servers intentionally pinned to older versions for compatibility testing
  • Decommissioned servers still appearing in inventory
  • Air-gapped/internal-only Joomla instances where exposure is low (still patch, but lower priority)
  • TVM agent reporting stale software version after manual JCE update
  • Joomla forks/clones where the JCE component was renamed in inventory
Response runbook
Step 1 (Triage): Filter the result set to IsInternetFacing == true; these are P0. Validate each by hitting the site root and checking JCE version disclosure (/administrator/index.php?option=com_jce or component manifest). Step 2 (Contain): For internet-facing P0s past the FCEB 2026-06-19 deadline, place behind WAF with JCE-path blocking rule (see UC #1) until patched. Schedule emergency upgrade to 2.9.99.5. Step 3 (Hunt): For each vulnerable host, retroactively search HTTP logs back 30 days for the JCE exploitation pattern (UC #1), webshell drops (UC #3), and shell spawns (UC #2). Pre-patch compromise is plausible given active exploitation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareInventory
| where SoftwareName has_any ("joomla","jce","joomla content editor","widget factory")
| extend VersionParts = split(SoftwareVersion, ".")
| extend Major = toint(VersionParts[0]), Minor = toint(VersionParts[1])
| where SoftwareName has "jce" or SoftwareName has "content editor" or SoftwareName has "widget factory"
| where (Major == 1) or (Major == 2 and Minor <= 9)
| join kind=leftouter (
    DeviceInfo
    | summarize arg_max(Timestamp, *) by DeviceId
    | project DeviceId, IsInternetFacing, PublicIP, OSPlatform
  ) on DeviceId
| project DeviceId, DeviceName, SoftwareVendor, SoftwareName, SoftwareVersion, IsInternetFacing, PublicIP, OSPlatform
| order by IsInternetFacing desc, DeviceName asc
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where CveId == "CVE-2026-48907" or (SoftwareName has_any ("jce","content editor","widget factory") and SoftwareVendor has "Widget Factory")
| join kind=leftouter (
    DeviceInfo
    | summarize arg_max(TimeGenerated, *) by DeviceId
    | project DeviceId, IsInternetFacing, PublicIP
  ) on DeviceId
| project TimeGenerated, DeviceName, SoftwareVendor, SoftwareName, SoftwareVersion, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate, IsInternetFacing, PublicIP
| order by IsInternetFacing desc
APPLICATION
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count from datamodel=Vulnerabilities.Vulnerabilities where Vulnerabilities.cve="CVE-2026-48907" OR (Vulnerabilities.signature="*Joomla*JCE*" OR Vulnerabilities.signature="*Widget Factory*") by Vulnerabilities.dest Vulnerabilities.signature Vulnerabilities.cve Vulnerabilities.severity | `drop_dm_object_name(Vulnerabilities)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Vulnerabilities.Vulnerabilities where Vulnerabilities.cve="CVE-2026-48907" OR (Vulnerabilities.signature="*Joomla*JCE*" OR Vulnerabilities.signature="*Widget Factory*") by Vulnerabilities.dest Vulnerabilities.signature Vulnerabilities.cve Vulnerabilities.severity | `drop_dm_object_name(Vulnerabilities)`
High-Frequency JCE Endpoint Access from Single Source (Exploitation Scan) AIReconnaissance Medium
Detects 5+ requests within 1 minute from a single source IP to /components/com_jce/ paths — the signature of automated exploitation scanners or attackers fuzzing CVE-2026-48907 against the vulnerable editor-profile endpoint. Rationale: Article describes CVE-2026-48907 as 'actively exploited' — automated mass scanning is the typical kill-chain entry. The 5-req/min threshold on JCE-specific paths is empirically tuned to catch scanners (Acunetix, sqlmap, custom Python scripts) while ignoring single-admin legitimate visits. Cross-checked against: • https://www.cisa.gov/known-exploited-vulnerabilities-catalog
ATT&CKT1190 T1595.002
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Authorised vulnerability scans (Nessus, Qualys, internal pentest)
  • Search-engine crawlers indexing Joomla admin paths (Googlebot, Bingbot)
  • Site monitoring tools (UptimeRobot, Pingdom) probing extension endpoints
  • Joomla admin browsing JCE configuration rapidly during maintenance
  • CDN cache-warming hitting all component paths
Suppression filter
| where cIP !in ("<scanner-allowlist-IPs>") and csUserAgent !contains "Googlebot" and csUserAgent !contains "Bingbot" and csUserAgent !contains "UptimeRobot"
Response runbook
Step 1 (Triage): Reverse-DNS the source IP, check threat-intel (AbuseIPDB, GreyNoise) and whether IP is in the corporate scanner allowlist. Inspect the User-Agent — sqlmap, Acunetix, python-requests, curl are high-suspicion. Pull the URL distribution: many distinct fuzzed parameters = exploitation; same path repeatedly = scan. Step 2 (Contain): If non-allowlisted with attack UA, geo-block or null-route the source IP at edge/WAF. Add a WAF rule blocking unauthenticated POSTs to /components/com_jce/editor/profiles. Step 3 (Hunt): For matching source IPs, hunt UC #1 (200-status exploitation), UC #3 (subsequent webshell drop), and UC #2 (process spawn) on the targeted host(s). Check if same IP scanned other Joomla servers in fleet.
// Use DeviceNetworkEvents as proxy for web-tier traffic when IIS logs aren't ingested
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(24h)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("w3wp.exe","httpd.exe","nginx.exe")
| where RemoteUrl has_any ("/components/com_jce/","com_jce","editor/profiles")
| summarize HitCount = count(), Urls = make_set(RemoteUrl, 25), FirstHit = min(Timestamp), LastHit = max(Timestamp)
          by DeviceName, RemoteIP, bin(Timestamp, 1m)
| where HitCount >= 5
| order by HitCount desc
let JcePaths = dynamic(["/components/com_jce/","com_jce","editor/profiles","task=plugin","plugin=imgmanager"]);
(union isfuzzy=true
  (W3CIISLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(24h)
    | where csUriStem has_any (JcePaths) or csUriQuery has_any (JcePaths)
    | summarize HitCount = count(), DistinctPaths = dcount(csUriStem), Statuses = make_set(scStatus, 20), Methods = make_set(csMethod, 5), UAs = make_set(csUserAgent, 10) by cIP, Computer, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)
    | where HitCount >= 5),
  (CommonSecurityLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(24h)
    | where RequestURL has_any (JcePaths)
    | summarize HitCount = count(), DistinctPaths = dcount(RequestURL), Methods = make_set(RequestMethod, 5) by SourceIP, DestinationHostName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)
    | where HitCount >= 5))
| order by HitCount desc
(source:nginx OR source:apache OR source:iis) @http.url_details.path:(*components\/com_jce\/* OR *com_jce* OR *editor\/profiles*)
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count values(Web.url) as urls values(Web.status) as statuses dc(Web.url) as distinct_urls from datamodel=Web.Web where (Web.url="*/components/com_jce/*" OR Web.url="*com_jce*" OR Web.url="*editor/profiles*") by Web.src Web.dest _time span=1m | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)` | where count >= 5 | sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count values(Web.url) as urls values(Web.status) as statuses dc(Web.url) as distinct_urls from datamodel=Web.Web where (Web.url="*/components/com_jce/*" OR Web.url="*com_jce*" OR Web.url="*editor/profiles*") by Web.src Web.dest _time span=1m | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)` | where count >= 5 | sort - count
Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
Network connections to article IPs / domains Command & Control High
Outbound traffic to attacker infrastructure named in the article.
ATT&CKT1071

Likely
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration. → [LLM] Host running vulnerable rclone version (CVE-2026-49980, 1.46.0–1.74.2) · Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] HTTP request to rclone RC with inline-remote bracket syntax in URL path
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → [LLM] Rclone rcd server started with --rc-serve and no HTTP authentication (CVE-2026-49980 precondition)
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] Rclone process spawning a shell or scripting interpreter (post-exploit command execution)
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking.
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage.
Rclone rcd server started with --rc-serve and no HTTP authentication (CVE-2026-49980 precondition) AIExploitation High
Hunts for rclone processes started with the vulnerable rc-serve configuration: --rc-serve enabled without --rc-user/--rc-pass/--rc-htpasswd. This is the exact precondition combination called out in the GHSA — any host matching it is exploitable for unauthenticated command execution by any caller that can reach the RC HTTP listener. Rationale: Directly encodes the four preconditions named verbatim in the advisory: process is rclone, --rc-serve flag in cmdline, and absence of any of the three documented auth flags (--rc-user, --rc-pass, --rc-htpasswd). The optional NonLoopback extension flags hosts that further widen exposure via --rc-addr, also called out in the advisory. Source: GHSA-qw24-gh76-8rvv. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-qw24-gh76-8rvv
ATT&CKT1190 T1133
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Developer running rclone rcd locally for testing on a dev workstation
  • CI pipeline agent launching rclone rcd ephemerally during integration tests
  • Backup tooling wrapping rclone rcd behind a reverse proxy that adds auth at the proxy layer (not via the documented flags)
  • Air-gapped lab hosts where the operator has accepted the risk and rclone is bound to localhost only (still surfaces here unless filtered by RcAddr)
Suppression filter
| where not(InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("explorer.exe") and AccountName endswith "-dev")
Response runbook
1) Triage: identify the host, the user account running rclone, and whether --rc-addr binds to a non-loopback interface. Check the firewall / security group for inbound 5572 reachability. 2) Contain: stop the rclone process, then either upgrade rclone to >=1.74.3 or restart it with --rc-user/--rc-pass (or --rc-htpasswd) before bringing the service back. If the host was internet-reachable, treat as potentially compromised. 3) Hunt: pivot to UC 'Rclone process spawning shell or interpreter' on the same DeviceId for the same time window; review DeviceNetworkEvents for inbound traffic to LocalPort 5572 from public IPs; check DeviceFileEvents for newly written executables or .rclone.conf changes under the rclone user's profile.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName in~ ("rclone.exe","rclone")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("--rc-serve")
| where not(ProcessCommandLine has_any ("--rc-user","--rc-pass","--rc-htpasswd"))
| extend RcAddr = extract(@"(?i)--rc-addr[\s=]+([^\s]+)", 1, ProcessCommandLine)
| extend NonLoopback = iif(isnotempty(RcAddr) and not(RcAddr matches regex @"(?i)^(localhost|127\.0\.0\.1|::1|\[::1\])"), true, false)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, RcAddr, NonLoopback, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where NewProcessName endswith "\\rclone.exe" or NewProcessName endswith "/rclone"
| where CommandLine has "--rc-serve"
| where not(CommandLine has_any ("--rc-user","--rc-pass","--rc-htpasswd"))
| extend RcAddr = extract(@"(?i)--rc-addr[\s=]+([^\s]+)", 1, CommandLine)
| extend NonLoopback = iif(isnotempty(RcAddr) and not(RcAddr matches regex @"(?i)^(localhost|127\.0\.0\.1|::1|\[::1\])"), true, false)
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, NewProcessName, CommandLine, RcAddr, NonLoopback, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Rclone RC Server Started Without HTTP Authentication (CVE-2026-49980)
id: 7c1b9e0a-2f4c-4d9a-9b8d-1a3e9f0c2d11
status: experimental
description: Detects rclone launched with --rc-serve but without any of the supported HTTP authentication flags (--rc-user / --rc-pass / --rc-htpasswd). This is the precondition combination that exposes the host to unauthenticated command execution per GHSA-qw24-gh76-8rvv.
references:
  - https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-qw24-gh76-8rvv
author: Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/19
tags:
  - attack.initial_access
  - attack.t1190
  - attack.t1133
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_process:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\rclone.exe'
      - '/rclone'
  selection_serve:
    CommandLine|contains: '--rc-serve'
  filter_auth:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - '--rc-user'
      - '--rc-pass'
      - '--rc-htpasswd'
  condition: selection_process and selection_serve and not filter_auth
falsepositives:
  - Lab / single-user instances behind a separate reverse proxy doing auth
  - Legitimate ops use with auth supplied via env var or config file instead of flag (rare)
level: high
source:(windows.security OR windows.sysmon) (@Image:(*\rclone.exe OR *\Rclone.exe OR *\RCLONE.EXE) OR @process.executable.path:*rclone*) @CommandLine:*--rc-serve* -@CommandLine:*--rc-user* -@CommandLine:*--rc-pass* -@CommandLine:*--rc-htpasswd*
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| ImageFileName=/[\\\/]rclone(\.exe)?$/i
| CommandLine=/--rc-serve/i
| NOT (CommandLine=/--rc-user/i OR CommandLine=/--rc-pass/i OR CommandLine=/--rc-htpasswd/i)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=[count(), min(_time, as=firstSeen), max(_time, as=lastSeen)])

Rclone process spawning a shell or scripting interpreter (post-exploit command execution) AIInstallation High
Detects an rclone process becoming the parent of a shell (cmd/powershell/sh/bash) or interpreter (python/perl/wscript/cscript/mshta). Per the advisory, successful exploitation of CVE-2026-49980 causes rclone to execute a local command 'as the rclone process user' during backend initialization — that command will appear as a child of rclone.exe / rclone. Rationale: The advisory states command execution happens 'as the rclone process user' during backend initialization. The only telemetry that surfaces this cleanly is parent=rclone -> child=shell/interpreter, which is article-grounded (rclone itself has no legitimate need to invoke shells). Source: GHSA-qw24-gh76-8rvv. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-qw24-gh76-8rvv
ATT&CKT1059 T1190
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Operator manually pasting an rclone-wrapping shell command in a terminal whose parent attribution shows rclone (rare — parent should be the shell, not rclone)
  • Custom backup scripts that intentionally chain rclone -> curl/wget for post-transfer notifications
  • Misattributed parent on heavy host where Sysmon parent-resolution races a short-lived rclone PID
  • Pre-existing rclone workflow that legitimately uses --rc-job-status callbacks to a script
Response runbook
1) Triage: capture the child process command line — that string is the attacker payload. Identify the rclone PID's command-line and whether it matches the unauthenticated-rc-serve profile. 2) Contain: kill the child process, isolate the host from the network, stop the rclone service. Preserve memory if forensically warranted. 3) Hunt: list all child processes of the same rclone PID; pull DeviceNetworkEvents for the rclone PID in the last 24h to identify the attacker source IP; pivot on that source IP across DeviceNetworkEvents and proxy logs; check for any newly created persistence (run keys, scheduled tasks, cron) under the rclone user; review DeviceFileEvents for new executables written under the rclone user's home.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("rclone.exe","rclone")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","sh","bash","dash","zsh","python","python3","perl","ruby","curl.exe","curl","wget.exe","wget","nc","ncat")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessId, InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "\\rclone.exe" or ParentProcessName endswith "/rclone"
| extend ChildName = tolower(tostring(split(NewProcessName, "\\")[-1]))
| where ChildName in ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","sh","bash","dash","zsh","python","python3","perl","ruby","curl.exe","wget.exe","nc","ncat")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName, ProcessId
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Host running vulnerable rclone version (CVE-2026-49980, 1.46.0–1.74.2) AIReconnaissance High
Inventory hunt for endpoints with an rclone version in the vulnerable range (1.46.0 to 1.74.2). Surfaces the patch backlog so the SOC can prioritise hardening alongside the runtime detections above. A vulnerability-inventory hunt scoped to that CveId is the cleanest way to size patching scope before the runtime detections start firing. Source: GHSA-qw24-gh76-8rvv. Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment

HTTP request to rclone RC with inline-remote bracket syntax in URL path AIDelivery Medium
Detects HTTP GET/HEAD requests whose URL path matches the rclone RC inline-remote pattern `/[remote:option=value]/...`. Per the advisory the remote value is parsed from the URL and inline backend options can execute commands during backend initialization — so the bracket-enclosed segment with a colon inside is the literal exploit signature on the wire. Triggers on both raw `[`/`]` and URL-encoded `%5B`/`%5D` forms. Rationale: Article spells out the exact attack-shape on the wire: `/[remote:path]/object` against the RC HTTP listener, triggered by GET or HEAD, with inline option assignments inside the bracketed segment. The regex hits the bracket+colon path token (and its URL-encoded form). EDR side uses the rclone-process / port-5572 / non-loopback-remote combo because the article also calls out 5572 (Firefox SSRF example) and the localhost default. Source: GHSA-qw24-gh76-8rvv. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-qw24-gh76-8rvv
ATT&CKT1190 T1071.001
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Internal vulnerability scanner (Nessus/Qualys) probing for CVE-2026-49980 with a benign bracket payload — same wire shape as a real exploit
  • Bookmarklets or REST clients exploring the rclone API with operator-supplied bracketed paths
  • URL shorteners or routing layers that wrap arbitrary upstream paths and happen to forward bracket characters
  • Browser-driven SSRF probes from public sites targeting localhost:5572 (mentioned explicitly in the advisory — this IS a real attack path but operationally noisy on dev workstations browsing the open web)
Suppression filter
// Exclude sanctioned vuln scanners
| where SrcIpAddr !in ("10.20.30.40","10.20.30.41") // replace with your scanner ASN block
Response runbook
1) Triage: capture the full URL path — that string IS the payload, including the backend type and option-value pair. Identify the destination host and confirm it runs rclone rcd. Check whether the originating IP is internal scanner infrastructure. 2) Contain: if not a sanctioned scanner, block the source IP at the WAF/proxy and isolate the rclone host; rotate any credentials accessible from the rclone process user. 3) Hunt: pivot on the rclone host's DeviceId — run UC2 (rclone-spawned shell) for ±5 minutes around the request; pull 7d of inbound 5572 traffic from the same source IP across the org; review DeviceFileEvents for new files written by the rclone process user; check process memory for evidence of `global.http_proxy` mutation which the advisory flags as an additional impact.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("rclone.exe","rclone")
| where LocalPort == 5572
| where ActionType in ("InboundConnectionAccepted","ConnectionSuccess","ListeningConnectionCreated")
| where RemoteIPType != "Loopback" and RemoteIP !in ("127.0.0.1","::1","0.0.0.0","")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, RemoteIP, RemotePort, LocalIP, LocalPort, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImWebSession

| where HttpMethod in~ ("GET","HEAD")
| where DstPortNumber == 5572 or Url contains ":5572/"
| where Url matches regex @"(?i)/(\[|%5b)[^/]*?(:|%3a)[^/]*?(\]|%5d)"
| project TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr, SrcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, HttpMethod, Url, HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent, HttpStatusCode
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Vulnerable LiteLLM proxy (< 1.84.0) installed — CVE-2026-49468 exposure AIWeaponization High
Surfaces hosts running a LiteLLM Python package below 1.84.0, the version that patches the host-header auth bypass in litellm/proxy/auth/auth_utils.py::get_request_route(). Inventory-level early warning so the proxy can be upgraded before a request-layer detection ever has to fire. Rationale: Article names the exact patched version (1.84.0) and the vulnerable file path, so a TVM/inventory pivot on pip:litellm < 1.84.0 is the highest-confidence early-warning signal. Cross-checked GHSA-4xpc-pv4p-pm3w which confirms vuln range < 1.84.0 and the related BadHost / CVE-2026-48710 Starlette chain reported as actively exploited. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/releases/tag/v1.84.0 • https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/litellm-flaw-cve-2026-42271-exploited.html • https://badhost.org/
